question: What draws the hierarchy lines of a selected unit and what H does; and what a headquarters' row of the unit panel shows.

addresses.name: KeyH_TogglesRenderHierarchy
addresses.no_signature: instructions inside a larger function, not a function entry
addresses.comment: **The H key.** In the game screen's key handler (rva 0x252540): `cmp cl, 0x68`, then GetGameSettings and the byte at +0xE8 (`render_hierarchy`) replaced by its opposite. The hierarchy lines are made or dropped on the next update. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Six instructions, 0x6537D2..0x6537EC: the compare with 0x68, the call of 0x45FF30, `cmp byte ptr [eax+0xe8], 0`, `sete cl`, the store.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_Rebuild
addresses.comment: **Makes the mesh of the hierarchy lines for a selected unit.** Counts the lines, makes a vertex buffer of four vertices a line (0x18 bytes each) and an index buffer of six indices a line, and fills them through HierarchyLines_AddBelow starting at the unit itself. Remembers the unit's commander at +0x10 and sets the byte +0x14; with no unit, or no line, clears it. The object is CInGameIdler +0x1DE0. The names of these five are ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: The counting walk (0x8829F0, 0x883AB0), `count * 4` and `0x18` to 0xAD4510, `count * 6` to 0xAD48B0, the two locks, the call of 0x883AF0 with the context whose fifth word is the unit. `ret 8`.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_IsCurrent
addresses.comment: Whether the mesh still fits: the unit's commander is the one remembered, and every unit the build would walk is the unit recorded at its place and in the province recorded with it. CInGameIdler::Update rebuilds when this answers false - so when a unit of the hierarchy changes province, or the selection or the order of battle changes. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 2.
addresses.evidence: The compare of [unit+0x1E0] with [lines+0x10], the walk through 0x882980 and 0x883A70 against the 8-byte records, the last compare of the count. Bare `ret`.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_AddBelow
addresses.comment: HierarchyLines_AddUnit on a unit, then itself on each unit under it (CUnit +0x1E4). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end: one call and one loop that recurses. Bare `ret`, two stack arguments cleaned by the caller.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_AddUnit
addresses.comment: Adds a unit's line to the mesh where it is a land unit aboard nothing, has a commander that (where a land unit) is aboard nothing either, and the two are in different provinces: from the unit point of its province to that of its commander's (CProvinceTemplate +0x64), with CUnit::IsOutOfRadioRange as the line's flag. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 3.
addresses.evidence: The tests of slot 15, of slot 9's +0x300 and +0x304, of [unit+0x1E0], the compare of the two [+0x130], the call of 0x5B6C00 and of 0x882B30 with `template + 100` twice. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_AddLine
addresses.signature: void __fastcall HierarchyLines_AddLine(void* context@ESI, CUnit* unit@EDX, int* from@stack:4, int* to@stack:8, bool outOfReach@stack:12)
addresses.comment: **One line of the hierarchy: four vertices and six indices.** Colour by the unit's place under the selected one: 0xFF007800 itself, 0xFF1432C8 directly under, 0xFF6464D2 two under, 0xFFC8C8C8 further, 0xFF800000 out of radio range. Half its width is (the counter size + 1) * 0.2 map pixels. The far end's v is length / (2 * half width) * 0.2; the fifth float of a vertex is 1.0 in reach and 0.0 out of it, which gfx/FX/hierarchy.fx turns into the sliding or the still half of its picture. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 4.
addresses.evidence: 0x882B36..0x882B8A for the five colours; the jump table on [unit+0x1F4] and the multiply by the double at 0x160A260 (0.2); the wrap by half the map's width; the four blocks of six stores at stride 0x18. `ret 0xC`.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_Draw
addresses.signature: void __stdcall HierarchyLines_Draw(void* camera, void* mesh, float phase)
addresses.comment: Draws the hierarchy's mesh with the effect hierarchy.fx: sets WorldViewProjectionMatrix, LineTexture and Time (the phase), and draws twice with two values of CameraPosition - by all appearance the two copies of the map either side of its seam. Called from the game screen's frame routine (rva 0x256E10) while render_hierarchy is on, counters are in view and the camera is under 500. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: The effect's handles at 0x1A8CB48..0x1A8CB58 used with its slots 32, 38, 52 and 30; the loop over the passes with two draws in each. `ret 0xC`.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_LoadShader
addresses.no_signature: `ret 4` with EBX read before it is written; what the one stack argument and EBX are was not worked out
addresses.comment: Loads the effect `/FX/hierarchy.fx`, its technique `Hierarchy`, the parameters WorldViewProjectionMatrix, CameraPosition, LineTexture and Time, the vertex declaration, and the texture `/mapitems/hierarchy_line.tga`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 5.
addresses.evidence: The literals, in that order, and the stores to 0x1A8CB44..0x1A8CB60.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::ShowSelection
addresses.comment: Slot 32. Clears what the last selection drew on the map - the markers of an AI's objectives, the arrows - and, for a unit of the player's, **gives its two counters their ring: 1, white, or 2, the counter type's color1, where an AI agent commands the unit or one above it**; then, for an AI-commanded unit, the objective markers and the AutomationArrow of its plan. Read as far as the ring; the name is ours. No caller passing 3 to CCounterObject::SetSelection was found. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: The two pairs of calls through the counters' slot 23 at [avatar+0x140] and [avatar+0x13C], with 1 and with 2, either side of the walk of +0x198 up +0x1E0. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CObjectivesEntry::CObjectivesEntry
addresses.no_signature: a constructor: the screen in ECX, the object and two more on the stack, read only at its one call site in CSingleUnitPanel::Rebuild
addresses.comment: A headquarters' row in the unit panel: the window `sup_objectives`, with the checkboxes `automate_checkbox`, `reorg_hq_checkbox` and `aggression_checkbox` registered. For a unit no AI commands it sets `aggression_slider` from 0x5D3F10 before the first update. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 10.
addresses.evidence: The four literals, the walk of +0x198 up +0x1E0, the call of 0x5D3F10 and the slider's slot 7. `ret 0xC`.

addresses.name: CObjectivesEntry::Update
addresses.comment: **The two faces of a headquarters' row.** No AI agent on the unit or above it: `automate_checkbox` clear, `reorg_hq_checkbox` and `objectives` hidden, the two `tac_aggro_` pictures, `aggression_checkbox` and `aggression_slider` shown - the box set from CUnit +0x4A, the slider locked while it is clear, and a CSetUnitAggressionCommand posted where a free slider has moved off CUnit +0x4C. An agent: the reverse, with `objectives` showing OBJECTIVES and the unit's objective, or NO_OBJECTIVES, and `reorg_hq_checkbox` set from CUnit +0x205. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 10.
addresses.evidence: The literals with the show (slot 13) and hide (slot 14) call after each, in the two branches of the test of +0x198; `operator_new(0x68)` and CSetUnitAggressionCommand behind the compare of the slider's value with [unit+0x4C]. Bare `ret`.

struct_fields.name: render_hierarchy
struct_fields.comment: the `render_hierarchy` key of the map rendering options, which sit at +0xDC: the hierarchy lines of a selected unit are drawn. The H key flips it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 1.
struct_fields.evidence: `ParseBool(parse, this + 0xC)` in CMapRenderingOptions::LoadKey's case for the key; the toggle at 0x6537DC and the reads at 0x657087 and 0x656625.

struct_fields.name: onmap
struct_fields.comment: the `onmap` key of the map rendering options. What reads it was not looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 1.

struct_fields.name: always_counters
struct_fields.comment: the `alwaysCounters` key of the map rendering options: counters, and with them the hierarchy lines, are drawn however near the camera is. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 1.
struct_fields.evidence: `ParseBool(parse, this + 0x1D)` in CMapRenderingOptions::LoadKey's case for alwaysCounters; the read at 0x657098 beside counter_distance.
struct_fields.revises: named for the key it now is known to be; it was counters_when_near, with which of two keys left open

struct_fields.name: show_unit_names
struct_fields.comment: the `show_unit_names` key of the map rendering options: a near counter's second text is the unit's name and not its leader's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 1.
struct_fields.evidence: `ParseBool(parse, this + 0xD)` in CMapRenderingOptions::LoadKey's case for show_unit_names.
struct_fields.revises: the comment only: the key is confirmed by the loader, where it was likely

struct_fields.name: hierarchy_lines
struct_fields.comment: the 0x40-byte object holding the mesh of the selected unit's hierarchy lines: the records it was built from at +0, the unit's commander at +0x10, a byte at +0x14 that there is something to draw, the picture's phase at +0x18, the mesh from +0x1C. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 2.
struct_fields.evidence: The store at 0x649334 after `operator_new` and the zeroing of +4..+0x3C; the reads in CInGameIdler::Update (0x6565A8, 0x65662E) and the frame routine (0x657076, 0x6570D9).

struct_fields.name: has_own_aggression
struct_fields.comment: the unit has an aggression setting of its own: the unit panel's `aggression_checkbox`. A parent's row marks such a unit with a coloured star. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 10.
struct_fields.evidence: The test of [unit+0x4A] before `aggression_checkbox` is set in 0x74E9F0, and before 0x5D3FE0 in CParentUnitEntry's constructor.

struct_fields.name: aggression
struct_fields.comment: the unit's aggression, fixed-point from -1 to 1: what the unit panel's `aggression_slider` is compared with before a CSetUnitAggressionCommand is posted, and what 0x5D3FE0 colours a parent row's star by (red over 0.1, blue under -0.1). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 10.
struct_fields.evidence: `slider value - [unit+0x4C]` in 0x74E9F0; the compares with floor(100.5) and floor(-99.5) in 0x5D3FE0.
